items.title: Bill Phillips Interview, 1961-05-24
items.q: He was sitting with Earl Hynden and they was waking on South Park about, uh, it was 39th in South Park. Grand Terrence.

ctx.x: Wait a minute. Oh. I can't think now. Ram. Ram. Ram. Very nice. I asked him a little bit about his brother, but he didn't tell us very much either. Can you tell us anything about his style of playing much?

Well, I don't know. I never pay too much attention. I seen him a lot of time down by the, um, um, place. No, uh, no, not in the Union Hall. I seen him a lot of time. He was sitting with Earl Hynden and they was waking on South Park about, uh, it was 39th in South Park. Grand Terrence. Grand Terrence. I seen him a lot of time down there waking up. You know, them fellas, you look at him, you're out having fun, you didn't come from playing, you ain't even stunned by him. You didn't have Joe nice waking up. Yeah,…
I never paid too much attention. He was playing with Johnny Dodds and Natty Dominique and I, I was paying more attention to Johnny Dodds the clarinetist then and didn't know a minor hall.
